headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and cascading errors; shared write access also creates medium data-leakage and capability-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP, while Prefect can orchestrate workflows that may consume those files or metadata. The shared filesystem and git bridge makes prompt injection plausible if Prefect ingests Claude-authored artifacts as instructions. No stronger channel is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect reads Claude-produced files or workflow metadata as instructions
IF both agents operate in the same working directory or git checkout
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable automatic parsing of agent-authored files
Require human review before Prefect consumes Claude outputs
Use provenance tags on generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, and has broad network egress. Prefect touches workflow metadata and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or environment material can flow from A into B’s outputs or external calls. The profiles do not prove default exfiltration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or git workspace
IF Prefect forwards workflow metadata derived from Claude-produced files to external services
mitigations: Use separate repositories or mounts
Redact secrets from files before Prefect reads them
Restrict network egress for one agent during shared runs
Rotate any exposed credentials after joint runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem and git only. Prefect is an orchestrator that can also mutate workflow state. That overlapping mutable surface makes concurrent writes and git-state races dangerous by default, with potential irreversible repo corruption or lost work.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git branch
IF Prefect and Claude run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Serialize writes through one operator
Use separate branches per agent
Add file-locking around shared paths
Pause one agent during commits
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, patches, and shell actions, while Prefect can orchestrate downstream workflow steps. If Prefect treats Claude output as authoritative, an error can cascade into automated actions or pipeline changes. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer higher severity is high.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Claude output without validation
IF Claude-produced artifacts are used to trigger workflow actions or deployments
mitigations: Require explicit validation before execution
Insert a human approval gate
Compare outputs against a schema or tests
Limit Prefect to read-only dry runs
requires-engineering: add signed artifacts and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, shell environment, and credentials, while Prefect handles workflow metadata. If regulated data or secrets are placed into the shared workflow, differing retention or residency expectations can be violated. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in shared workflow metadata
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared metadata
Minimize logging of sensitive fields
Document retention settings for both systems
Delete test artifacts after runs
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
